Cyclization & Anomeric Carbon ($C_1$ in Aldoses; $C_2$ in Ketoses)
quickSummary: Carbohydrates are polyhydroxy aldehydes (aldoses like D-Glucose) or ketones (ketoses like D-Fructose). Epimers differ in configuration at a single chiral center (C-2: Glucose & Mannose; C-4: Glucose & Galactose). Hexose cyclization creates a new asymmetric center at C-1 (anomeric carbon): α-anomer has the -OH group below the Haworth ring; β-anomer has the -OH group above the ring.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.1 Stereochemistry, Epimers, & Anomers
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.1 Stereochemistry, Epimers, & Anomers
conceptBreakdown.content:
### Epimeric Relationships
Epimers are diastereomers differing in configuration around a single asymmetric carbon:
• **C-2 Epimers**: $\text{D}$-Glucose and $\text{D}$-Mannose.
• **C-4 Epimers**: $\text{D}$-Glucose and $\text{D}$-Galactose.

### Anomers ($\alpha$ vs $\beta$ Forms)
Intramolecular hemiacetal cyclization creates a new chiral center at **C-1 (the Anomeric Carbon)**:
• **$\alpha$-Anomer**: Hydroxyl ($-\text{OH}$) group at $\text{C}-1$ lies **below** the Haworth ring plane.
• **$\beta$-Anomer**: Hydroxyl ($-\text{OH}$) group at $\text{C}-1$ lies **above** the Haworth ring plane.
